Regulations and policy
I.F.R. fuel requirements.
Enough fuel must be carried to complete the flight to the first airport of intended landing, fly from that airport to the alternate airport, and fly after that for 45 minutes at normal cruising speed. Reference. one thirty five, two 23, A.
When do you not need an alternate for your destination?
For one hour before or after the expected time of arrival, the ceiling must be at least 1,500 feet above the lowest circling approach Minimum Descent Altitude, or If a circling instrument approach procedure is not authorized, the ceiling must be at least 1,500 feet above the lowest ceiling minimums or 2,000 feet above airport elevation, whichever is higher, and The visibility must be forecast to be at least 3 statute miles, or 2 statute miles more than the lowest applicable visibility minimums, whichever is greater, for the instrument approach procedure to be used at the destination airport. Reference. one thirty five, two 23, B.
Alternate Airport I.F.R. Weather Minimums.
For airports with at least one operational navigational facility providing a straight in, non precision, or CAT one precision, approach procedure, add 400 feet to the minimum descent altitude or height, or decision altitude or height, and add one statute mile or 1600 meters to the landing minimum. For airports with at least two operational navigational facilities, each providing a straight in approach procedure to different suitable runways, add 200 feet to the minimum descent altitude or height, or decision altitude or height, and add one half statute mile or 800 meters to the landing minimum. If appropriately equipped, you may use a G.P.S. based instrument approach procedures at both the destination and an alternate airport. However, At the alternate, only L-NAV or circling M.D.A.'s are to be planned for unless equipped with baro V-NAV. Reference. Op Spec Charlie fifty five.
IFR takeoff minimums
Standard takeoff minimums are 1 statute mile or R.V.R 5000 for aircraft having two engines or less, and one half statute mile or R.V.R 2400 for airplanes having more than 2 engines. Additionally, the certificate holder is authorized to use a takeoff minimum equal to the lowest authorized straight-in Category one I.F.R. landing minimum applicable to the certificate holder for that particular airport. Touchdown R.V.R report, if available is controlling. If a higher than standard takeoff minimum is published and no alternate procedure is prescribed, that higher published takeoff minimum is controlling. The note prohibiting single-engine I.F.R. part 135 passenger-carrying operations, in lower than standard takeoff minimums, only applies to non turbine single-engine aircraft. Reference. Op Spec Charlie fifty seven.
When is a takeoff alternate required?
If the required weather conditions are above takeoff minimums, but below authorized I.F.R. landing minimums, you must have an alternate airport within 1 hour's flying time, at normal cruising speed in still air, of the departure airport. Reference. one 35, two 17.
Continuing an approach at the destination.
Must have the required approach minimums in order to continue an instrument approach, unless the aircraft is already established on the final approach segment of the approach. Upon arriving at the MDA or DA you must have the required weather minimums in order to land. Reference. 135, two 25.
Requirements for descending below the Decision or minimum descent altitudes. You need to have any of the following in sight. the runway or environment. the approach lighting system. the threshold marking or lighting. the runway end identifier lights. the VASI. the touchdown zone markings or lights. and the runway markings or lights. Additionally, you need the required flight visibility and can make a normal approach and landing. Reference. 91, one 75.
Relevant Approach Category speeds.
Category B. 91 to 121 knots. Category C. 121 to 141 knots. For Guardian Flight, approach speed standards are V-REF to V-REF plus 10 knots.
Circling approach radius distance.
Standard Circling Approach Maneuvering radius. Category B, 1.5 nautical miles. Category C, 1.7 Nautical miles. Expanded Circling Approach maneuvering radius. M.D.A .of 1000 feet or less. 1.7 nautical miles for Cat B. 2.7 nautical miles for Cat C. M.D.A .of 1001 to 3000 feet. 1.8 nautical miles for Cat B. 2.8 nautical miles for Cat C. M.D.A. of 3001 to 5000 feet. 1.8 nautical miles for Cat B. 2.9 nautical miles for Cat C. M.D.A. of 5001 to 7000 feet. 1.9 nautical miles for Cat B. 3.0 nautical miles for Cat C. M.D.A. of 7001 to 9000 feet. 2.0 nautical miles for Cat B. 3.2 nautical miles for Cat C. M.D.A. of 9001 feet and above. 1.9 nautical miles for Cat B. 3.0 nautical miles for Cat C.
Land and hold short restrictions.
- Landing distance should be A.F.M. plus 1000 feet. - No wet runways. - The runway must have electronic or visual approach guidance. - Weather of no less than a 1500 foot ceiling, and a visibility of no less than 5 statute miles. - Weather can be reduced to 1000 and 3 if a PAPI or VASI is installed and operational. - Where a rejected landing procedure is published, weather minima will be published in local flying directives. - LAH SO is not authorized if wind shear is reported in the 20 minutes prior to the LAH SO clearance. - Tailwind should be calm or less than 3 knots. - Night LAH SO only with approved LAH SO lighting installed. - Reference, Op spec Alpha 27.
Lost communication procedures.
If under V.F.R. conditions, continue the flight under V.F.R. and land as soon as practicable. Otherwise, if under I.F.R. conditions. Transponder set to 7600. Route, Cleared, Vectored, Expected, Filed. Altitude, highest of Assigned, Minimum en route, expected altitude. Reference. one 35, one 85.
One thirty five V.F.R. minimums
V.F.R. minimum altitudes. Daytime, 500 feet above the surface and 500 feet horizontally from any obstacle. At night, 1000 feet above the highest obstacle within 5 miles of the course to be flown or 2000 feet in mountainous terrain. V.F.R. minimum visibility. In uncontrolled airspace, not less than 1000 feet ceilings unless the flight visibility is at least 2 miles. Reference one thirty five two zero three and two zero five.
Airspace speed Limits
Speed limit below 10000 feet. 250 knots. Speed limit below class Bravo airspace or a V.F.R. corridor. 200 knots. Speed limit for class Charlie or Delta. 200 knots within 4 nautical miles and up to 2500 A. G. L. Reference. 91, one 17.
One Thirty Five Oxygen Requirements
For pilots. At MSL altitudes or cabin altitudes above 10000 through 12000 feet. Continuously after 30 minutes. Above 12000. Continuously. For passengers. At MSL altitudes or cabin altitudes above 10000 through 15000 feet. Available to supply at least 10% of passengers after 30 minutes at those altitudes. Above 15000 feet. Supplied to all passengers. Above 25000 feet in pressurized aircraft. At least a 10 minute supply to all occupants of the aircraft, for use in the event of the loss of cabin pressurization.
Reference one thirty five, eighty nine and one fifty seven.
Flight hour limits, unscheduled operations.
8 hours per day 500 hours per quarter 800 hours every 2 consecutive quarters 1400 hours per calendar year Rest requirements. 10 hours of rest within the preceding 24 hours to the start of duty. Reference, one thirty five, two sixty seven.
Multi engine aircraft load manifest requirement.
A load manifest must be prepared prior to each flight for multi engine aircraft. A copy of this record must be carried in the aircraft to it's destination and copy maintained by the certificate holder for at least 30 days. Reference, one thirty five, 63.
Medical certificate duration.
First Class, 12 calendar months if under 40 and 6 months if 40 or older. Second class, 12 calendar months. Third class, 60 calendar months if under 40 and 24 calendar months if 40 or older. Reference 61, 23.
Pre-takeoff contamination check.
At any time the conditions are such that frost, ice, or snow may be reasonably expected to adhere to the aircraft, a Pre-takeoff contamination check must be completed within 5 minutes of takeoff, in order to ensure that critical surfaces are free of contamination. Reference Op spec Alpha 41.
M.E.L. category duration
Category A. Defined in M.E.L. Category B. 3 days. Category C. 10 days. Category D. 120 days.
Documents required. Airworthiness certificate, Aircraft registration, Radio station license for flights outside of the US, Operating limitations, weight and balance data, avionics manuals, company issued electronic flight bag, aircraft maintenance logbook.
Transponder emergency codes.
75 hundred, Hijacking. 76 hundred, Radio failure. 77 hundred, general emergency.
Width of a victor airway. 8 nautical miles, 4 miles on either side of the center. Standard holding pattern turning direction. To the right. Information to report to A.T.C. upon entering a hold. Time and altitude reaching the clearance limit. Begin slowing to holding speed within 3 minutes or less. 3 degree Glide slope calculation. Half of your ground speed multiplied by 10.
